newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian shares down in record turnover.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian shares down in record turnover.

text.p: Palestinian shares closed slightly lower on Tuesday as trading volume reached its highest level since the bourse opened in February, a Palestine Securities Exchange (PSE) report said.
The report said 454,250 shares valued at 809,845 Jordanian dinars changed hands during the PSE's 19th weekly trading session, an 800 percent increase on the previous week's record 66,401 shares.

"This is just a natural increase in trading in the initial stages of the capital market as more trading counters open and more participants enter the market," PSE General Manager Safwan Bataina told Reuters.

Trading in Palestine Telecommunications Co accounted for nearly 75 percent of Tuesday's turnover. Gaza al-Ahlia Insurance Co closed down 2.5 percent at $1.17 per share against $1.20 the previous week.
Al-Quds Bank for Development and Investment dropped 1.92 percent to $1.02 against $1.04 last week and Palestine International Bank slipped to 1.08 dinars from 1.10 dinars the previous session.
Shares are traded in Jordanian dinars and U.S. dollars in the absence of a Palestinian currency.
"Prices are mostly holding their levels," Bataina said. "There's still not enough liquidity and breadth."

The stock exchange opened in February with a once weekly trading session. The PSE plans to move to twice-a-week trading starting July 13. Officials say an index will be published after the number of companies traded reaches 15. -- Daniel Sternoff, Jerusalem newsroom, 972-2-537-0502
